THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.10.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
3  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant/third respondent, insurer of the offending vehicle, challenging the impugned award dated 27.09.2014 in O.P.(MV) No.1371 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Palakkad.
The respondents herein are the respondents 1, 2 and 4 before the tribunal.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 17.04.2010 at about 5.45 p.m., while the claimant was standing at the edge of the road at Eduppukulam, a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-9/B-9349 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the claimant, and as a result, he sustained serious injuries.

The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1,48,000/-.
3.

Before the tribunal, the first respondent, registered owner of the offending motorcycle contended that he was not 2025:KER:74335 MACA NO. 3375 OF 2015 the owner in possession of the offending vehicle on the relevant date of accident, since he had sold the vehicle on 20.11.2002.
Though entered appearance, the second respondent, the rider of the motorcycle, did not file any written statement.

The third respondent, who was the insurer of the offending vehicle filed a written statement,
admitting the insurance policy and disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
They contended that the second respondent, the rider of the motorcycle, was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
The owner in possession of the offending vehicle on the date of accident was impleaded as the supplemental fourth respondent in the original petition.
He contended that the person who was actually in possession of the vehicle was another person with the same name.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A8 and Exts.B1, X1, X1(a) and XI (b) were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, found that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part 2025:KER:74335 MACA NO. 3375 OF 2015 of the second respondent and awarded a sum of 66,300/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs against the third respondent being the insurer.

sentences.text: vehicle
for non-production of the driving licence, the third respondent insurance company has come up in appeal.

4. I have heard the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant insurance company and the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent/the owner of the vehicle.
5.

According to the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/insurer, a specific contention was raised before the tribunal that the rider of the motorcycle was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Though an I.A.No.2593 of 2011 was filed directing the owner and the rider of the vehicle to produce the driving licence, they failed to 2025:KER:74335 MACA NO. 3375 OF 2015 do so.
It is also submitted that the police had charge-sheeted against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence under Section 3(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Even then the tribunal erred in allowing the right of recovery from the owner of the vehicle stating that the original policy was not produced before the tribunal.
The learned Standing Counsel further submits that,
along with the appeal, a true copy of the policy was produced as per I.A.No.4316/2015

. 
6. The learned counsel appearing for the first respondent, owner, submits that the motorcycle bearing registration No.KL- 9/B-9349 was transferred in the name of supplemental 4 th respondent.
The learned counsel also submits that, before the tribunal, it was specifically contended in the written statement that the vehicle had been transferred.
It is on the basis of the written statement filed by the first respondent, the tribunal had not granted the right of recovery against the owner of the vehicle.
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the insurer had specifically contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
It is also noted that the police had charge-sheeted against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence under Section 3(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

However, the tribunal, in paragraph 11 of the award has observed that, since the third respondent - insurer did not produce the policy before the tribunal, whether there was any violation of policy condition could not be considered.

It is also noted that no document has been produced by the owner of the vehicle to prove that the registration certificate of the vehicle was transferred in the name of supplemental third respondent in the appeal.

The true copy of the policy produced along with the appeal, very clearly states that the insured person must ensure that the driver should hold a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
However, the driving licence of the rider of the 2025:KER:74335 MACA NO. 3375 OF 2015 motorcycle was not produced.
Since there was no valid driving licence, there was violation of policy conditions and the insurer is entitled for right of recovery of the amount awarded by the tribunal.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned award dated 27.09.2014 in O.P.(MV) No.
1371/2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Palakkad, is modified to the extent that, on payment of the amount awarded, the insurer will be at liberty to recover the said amount from the first respondent/ owner of the vehicle.
It is also made clear that the insurer will be at liberty to recover the statutory amount already deposited before the tribunal.
